newsitem.title: UK: Diana tantalises Britons with hint of big surprise.
newsitem.headline: Diana tantalises Britons with hint of big surprise.

text.p: Princess Diana, the royal superstar who once tearfully claimed she wanted to be alone, tantalised Britons on Tuesday with the promise of a shock announcement about her future.

In an extraordinary speedboat rendezvous with British journalists spying on her supposedly private holiday in the south of France, Diana revealed her teenage sons had urged her to quit Britain for a quieter life elsewhere.
Clad only in a leopard print swimsuit and sunglasses, the 36-year old princess was then pictured leaning over a yacht on Monday and reportedly telling the press corps;
"You are going to get a big surprise, you'll see. You are going to get a big surprise with the next thing I do," and promised a statement within two weeks.
Diana's London office issued a statement on Tuesday saying that "there was no discussion of the possibility of any statement being issued in the future".
But the damage was already done.

Newspapers and royal pundits went into overdrive with speculation about the latest bombshell in Diana's armoury of surprises, ranging from her 1995 admission on television of adultery to her 1993 withdrawal from public life.
Bookmakers William Hill started taking bets on options including re-marriage (6-4), becoming a nun (25-1) and joining the Spice Girls pop group (1,000-1).
"It was a very volatile outburst," said Ingrid Seward, editor in chief of Majesty magazine.

Diana's speedboat dash across the Mediterranean to the boat carrying the press corps was ostensibly a plea for privacy after severe criticism at home for holidaying with Egyptian-born Harrods boss Mohammed al-Fayed.

Al Fayed was at the centre of a sleaze scandal that helped crush the previous Conservative government after he revealed that he had paid several MPs thousands of pounds (dollars) to ask questions in parliament on his behalf.
"My boys are urging me continually to leave the country. They say it is the only way," Diana was quoted as saying.
"Maybe that's what I should do. They want me to live abroad. I sit in London all the time and I am abused and followed wherever I go. Now I am being forced to move from here," the princess added.
A move abroad, possibly to France, Italy or New York, was mooted following Diana's acrimonious divorce almost a year ago from heir to the throne Prince Charles.

But if Diana did quit Britain she would have to leave her two beloved sons behind. Fifteen-year-old Prince William is next in line to the throne after Charles and for security and protocol reasons would not be allowed to live abroad.
Other royal watchers believe re-marriage is on the cards for Diana, who has been romantically linked with several eligible men over the past year.

Last month, Diana was forced to issue a formal denial that she had become engaged to heart specialist Hasnat Khan, the 38-year-old doctor at Britain's Harefield Hospital who helped organise her controversial filmed attendance at an operation last year.
"The only big shock she could surprise us with is that she is marrying again and Doctor Khan is in the frame," said Hello magazine's royal correspondent Judy Wade.
"He has been involved with her for 18 months but she has been very clever at keeping us from seeing them together," Wade added.
Diana's bizarre encounter at sea underlined her penchant for stealing the limelight while at the same time professing her distate for her role of the world's most photographed woman.

Just as she grabbed the front-pages by wearing a stunning off the shoulder cocktail dress on the night in 1994 that Charles went public about his affair with Camilla Parker Bowles, Diana has again reduced the rest of the royal family to also-rans.
"The interesting thing is the timing. Her timing is impeccable. She has knocked Al Fayed out of the headlines and turned the spoltight back on herself," said Wade.
"Who remembers now about Camilla having a 50th birthday party this week, or about the queen's golden wedding anniversary garden party? It's very clever," she said.
